learn.title: Resources, resource groups, subscriptions, management groups
objectives: Describe Azure resources and resource groups and the rules that govern them.
Explain what a subscription is and why organisations use more than one.
Describe management groups and how they organise subscriptions.
Place each level in the hierarchy and explain how settings are inherited downwards.
Choose the right level to apply access, policy and billing separation.
concepts: Resource
Any manageable item you create in Azure: a VM, storage account, virtual network, database, web app.
Resource group
A logical container for resources that share a lifecycle. Every resource belongs to exactly one resource group. Resource groups can't be nested.
Resource group location
The region where the resource group's metadata is stored. Resources inside it can be in other regions.
Deleting a resource group
Deletes every resource inside it. That makes resource groups handy for removing a whole test environment at once.
Subscription
A unit of management, billing and scale. Resources and resource groups live inside a subscription. It is both a billing boundary and an access-control boundary.
Entra tenant link
A subscription trusts exactly one Microsoft Entra tenant for identities. One tenant can be trusted by many subscriptions.
Management group
A container above subscriptions used to apply governance (Azure Policy, RBAC) to many subscriptions at once.
Root management group
A single top-level management group per tenant. All management groups and subscriptions sit under it.
Hierarchy depth
Management groups can be nested up to six levels deep, not counting the root level or the subscription level.
Inheritance
Policies and role assignments applied at a level flow down to everything beneath it: management group → subscription → resource group → resource.
comparisons: A resource group organises resources by lifecycle. A subscription separates billing, access and limits.
A subscription holds resources. A management group holds subscriptions (and other management groups) for governance only.
An account is the identity that signs in. A subscription is the billing and resource container the account has access to. One account can use many subscriptions.
A region is a physical geography. A resource group is a logical grouping that can contain resources from many regions.
traps: Resource groups can't contain other resource groups.
A resource can't be in two resource groups at once.
The resource group's region doesn't restrict where its resources are deployed.
Management groups don't hold resources directly. They hold subscriptions and other management groups.
Each subscription or management group has exactly one parent.
Tags aren't inherited by default, but policies and role assignments are.
revision: Hierarchy: management group → subscription → resource group → resource.
Apply settings high to affect many, low to affect few.
Separate subscriptions for separate billing, environments or limits.
Delete the resource group to delete everything in it.
One root management group per tenant; up to six levels of nesting below it.
A subscription trusts one Entra tenant.

questions.on: Describe Azure resources and resource groups
questions.q: In Azure, what is a resource?
opts: A manageable item you create in Azure, such as a virtual machine, storage account or virtual network
A physical server that Microsoft assigns to one customer
A user account in Microsoft Entra ID
A billing invoice produced each month
questions.e: Resources are the building blocks you deploy and manage through Azure Resource Manager.

questions.on: Describe Azure resources and resource groups
questions.q: How many resource groups can a single Azure resource belong to at the same time?
opts: Up to two
As many as needed
Exactly one
Up to ten

questions.on: Describe Azure resources and resource groups
questions.q: Is this statement true or false? 'You can place a resource group inside another resource group to build a folder structure.'
opts: True, but only inside the same region
True. Up to three levels of nesting are allowed
False. Resource groups can only be nested inside management groups
False. Resource groups can't be nested
questions.e: Resource groups are a single flat layer. Use management groups and subscriptions for higher-level structure.

questions.on: Describe Azure resources and resource groups
questions.q: What happens to the resources inside a resource group when the resource group is deleted?
opts: They are all deleted
They move to the subscription's root
They move to a default resource group
They stay running but become unmanaged

questions.on: Describe Azure resources and resource groups
questions.q: A team builds a temporary training lab with VMs, a virtual network and a storage account. All of it must be removed together when the course ends. How should the team organise these resources?
opts: Put each resource in its own subscription
Spread the resources across several existing production resource groups
Create a management group for the lab and put the resources in it directly
Place all the lab resources in one dedicated resource group
questions.e: Resources that share a lifecycle belong in the same resource group, so you can delete them in one step.

questions.on: Describe Azure resources and resource groups
questions.q: A resource group was created in the West Europe region. Where can the resources inside it be deployed?
opts: Only in West Europe or its paired region
In any Azure region, because the resource group's location only stores its metadata
Only in West Europe
Only in regions within the same geography
questions.e: The resource group's region is where its metadata is kept. Its resources can be in other regions.

questions.on: Describe Azure resources and resource groups
questions.q: A company has a rule that resource management metadata must stay in Europe. Its resource groups are all created in European regions, but some resources are in US regions. What does choosing a European region for each resource group achieve?
opts: The US resources are blocked from running
The resources' data is replicated to Europe
All the resources are automatically moved to Europe
Each resource group's metadata, which describes its resources, is stored in that European region
questions.e: The resource group location controls where its metadata lives, not where the resources or their data run.

questions.on: Describe Azure resources and resource groups
questions.q: An administrator moves a storage account from one resource group to another in the same subscription. What happens to the storage account's region?
opts: It stays in the same region; only its resource group changes
It moves to the new resource group's region
It moves to the paired region
It is recreated in a random region

questions.on: Describe Azure resources and resource groups
questions.q: The marketing team should be able to manage only the resources for its campaign website. Which approach is simplest?
opts: Give the team a role on each individual resource across all resource groups
Give the team Owner on the whole subscription
Create a separate Entra tenant for marketing
Put the website's resources in one resource group and give the team a role on that resource group
questions.e: Role assignments at resource group scope are inherited by every resource in the group.

questions.on: Describe subscriptions
questions.q: Which description of an Azure subscription is correct?
opts: A physical datacenter allocated to one customer
A single virtual machine with a monthly fee
A logical container that provides billing and access-control boundaries for the resources it holds
A security group of users in Microsoft Entra ID

questions.on: Describe subscriptions
questions.q: A company's finance department wants a completely separate Azure bill for each of its three business units. What should it use?
opts: A separate region for each business unit
A separate resource group for each business unit in one subscription
A separate virtual network for each business unit
A separate subscription for each business unit
questions.e: Billing reports and invoices are generated per subscription, so separate subscriptions give separate bills.

questions.on: Describe subscriptions
questions.q: A company wants to make sure developers can never see or touch production resources, even by accident. What gives the cleanest separation?
opts: Use separate subscriptions for development and production
Use one resource group for both, with different names for each resource
Use separate regions for development and production
Use separate tags for development and production
questions.e: A subscription is an access-control boundary: access granted in one doesn't apply to another.

questions.on: Describe subscriptions
questions.q: How many Microsoft Entra tenants does an Azure subscription trust for identities at any one time?
opts: Up to two
As many as are linked to the billing account
Exactly one
Up to five

questions.on: Describe subscriptions
questions.q: Is this statement true or false? 'One Microsoft Entra tenant can be trusted by many Azure subscriptions.'
opts: False. Each tenant can have only one subscription
True. Many subscriptions can trust the same tenant, but each subscription trusts only one
True, but only if all subscriptions are in the same region
False. Tenants and subscriptions aren't related

questions.on: Describe subscriptions
questions.q: What is the relationship between an Azure account and Azure subscriptions?
opts: A subscription can only ever be used by one account
Each account can have exactly one subscription
Accounts and subscriptions are the same thing
One account can have access to one or more subscriptions

questions.on: Describe subscriptions
questions.q: A large project expects to exceed some of the resource quotas of a single subscription. What's a common way to handle this?
opts: Spread the workload across additional subscriptions
Move the resources to a different region in the same subscription
Create more resource groups in the same subscription to raise the limits
Nest the subscription inside another subscription
questions.e: Quotas and limits apply per subscription, so scale-out across subscriptions is a standard pattern.

questions.on: Describe subscriptions
questions.q: Which is a common reason to create more than one subscription?
opts: To create a second root management group
To separate environments such as development, test and production
To let a resource belong to two resource groups
To allow virtual machines to run in more regions

questions.on: Describe management groups
questions.q: What is the main purpose of an Azure management group?
opts: To manage access, policy and compliance across multiple subscriptions
To provide a separate invoice for each resource
To hold virtual machines directly
To replicate data between regions

questions.on: Describe management groups
questions.q: What can a management group contain?
opts: Only resource groups
Only users and groups from Entra ID
Subscriptions and other management groups
Resources and resource groups directly

questions.on: Describe management groups
questions.q: How many root management groups does each Microsoft Entra tenant have?
opts: One per subscription
One
Up to six
One per region

questions.on: Describe management groups
questions.q: How deep can a management group hierarchy be?
opts: Up to three levels, including the root
Up to ten levels, including subscriptions
There is no depth limit
Up to six levels, not counting the root level or the subscription level
questions.e: Microsoft documents a maximum of six levels of depth below the root, excluding the subscription level.

questions.on: Describe management groups
questions.q: Is this statement true or false? 'A subscription can be placed under two management groups at the same time so that both groups' policies apply.'
opts: False. Subscriptions can't be placed in management groups
False. Each subscription has exactly one parent management group
True. Up to two parents are allowed
True, but only for pay-as-you-go subscriptions

questions.on: Describe management groups
questions.q: A company has 40 subscriptions. It wants one Azure Policy that restricts deployments to EU regions to apply to all of them, including subscriptions created later under the same structure. Where should it assign the policy?
opts: Separately on each of the 40 subscriptions
On one resource group in each subscription
On the billing account
At a management group that contains all the subscriptions
questions.e: Policies assigned to a management group are inherited by every subscription beneath it, including new ones.

questions.on: Describe the hierarchy of resource groups, subscriptions, and management groups
questions.q: Which order lists the Azure organisation levels from highest to lowest?
opts: Subscription, management group, resource group, resource
Management group, subscription, resource group, resource
Management group, resource group, subscription, resource
Resource group, subscription, management group, resource

questions.on: Describe the hierarchy of resource groups, subscriptions, and management groups
questions.q: A role assignment is made at a subscription. Which resources does it affect?
opts: The management group above the subscription as well
Only the resource groups, not the resources inside them
Only resources created after the assignment
All resource groups and resources in that subscription

questions.on: Describe the hierarchy of resource groups, subscriptions, and management groups
questions.q: An auditor needs read-only access to every resource in all of the company's subscriptions, and nothing more. What's the most efficient way to grant it?
opts: Assign the Reader role at the management group that contains all the subscriptions
Create a new subscription and move all resources into it
Assign the Reader role on every resource individually
Assign the Owner role at the root management group
questions.e: Granting the least-privilege role at the highest common scope covers everything below it through inheritance.

questions.on: Describe Azure resources and resource groups
questions.q: Which statement about resource groups and regions is correct?
opts: A resource group becomes a region when it has more than 100 resources
One resource group can contain resources from several regions
A resource group can only contain resources from its own region
Each region automatically gets one resource group

questions.on: Describe the hierarchy of resource groups, subscriptions, and management groups
questions.q:
Evaluate these statements.
1. A resource group can contain other resource groups.
2. A management group can contain other management groups.
3. A subscription can contain resource groups.
Which statements are true?
opts: Statements 2 and 3 only
Statement 3 only
Statements 1, 2 and 3

questions.on: Describe Azure resources and resource groups
questions.q: When you create a new virtual machine in Azure, what must you choose or create as part of the deployment?
opts: A management group to hold the VM
A separate Entra tenant for the VM
A resource group to hold the VM

questions.on: Describe Azure resources and resource groups
questions.q: An engineer deleted a resource group to remove one old test VM, and a production database in the same group was deleted too. What design change best prevents this in future?
opts: Group resources by lifecycle, so production resources aren't in the same resource group as temporary ones
Use a separate Entra tenant for the database
Store the database in a different region within the same resource group
Put every resource in the root management group
questions.e: Deleting a resource group removes everything in it, so mixed lifecycles in one group are risky. Resource locks (Session 19) add another safeguard.

questions.on: Describe Azure resources and resource groups
questions.q: A company reorganises and needs a web app and its database to be billed to a different department. Both departments use separate subscriptions. What can the administrator do?
opts: Nothing; resources can never leave the subscription they were created in
Move the resources to a resource group in the other subscription, where the resource types support moving
Assign a tag that changes which subscription is billed
Change the resources' region to switch billing
questions.e: Many resource types can be moved between resource groups and subscriptions. Some have restrictions, so check support first.

questions.on: Describe Azure resources and resource groups
questions.q: Is this statement true or false? 'A tag applied to a resource group is automatically applied to every resource inside it.'
opts: False. Tags aren't inherited by default, although Azure Policy can be used to apply them
True. Tags always flow down to child resources
False. Resource groups can't have tags
True, but only for virtual machines
questions.e: Unlike policies and role assignments, tags don't inherit automatically.

questions.on: Describe management groups
questions.q: A global company wants separate governance rules for its Europe and Americas divisions, with each division owning several subscriptions. Which structure fits?
opts: One region for each division
One resource group for each division in a shared subscription
A management group for each division, with that division's subscriptions inside it
One virtual network for each division

questions.on: Describe subscriptions
questions.q: Which of these is a type of Azure subscription offer?
opts: Resource group plan
Pay-as-you-go
Management group licence
Availability zone plan

questions.on: Describe subscriptions
questions.q: At which level does Azure generate invoices for resource usage?

Availability zone
Management group

questions.on: Describe management groups
questions.q: Which is NOT a purpose of management groups?

Assigning role-based access across many subscriptions

questions.on: Describe management groups
questions.q: A new subscription is created in a tenant that uses management groups, and no one places it anywhere specific. Where does it appear by default?

Inside the resource group of the person who created it
Under the root management group (or the default management group the tenant has configured)

questions.on: Describe the hierarchy of resource groups, subscriptions, and management groups
questions.q: A policy that denies a VM size is assigned at a management group. A subscription owner beneath it tries to create a VM of that size. What happens?
opts: It succeeds, but an email is sent to the administrator
The deployment is denied, because the policy is inherited by the subscription
It succeeds, because policies only apply to resources that existed when assigned

questions.on: Describe subscriptions
questions.q: A university wants its research, teaching and administration departments to manage their own Azure spend and access independently. Which approach is the most typical starting point?

questions.on: Describe the hierarchy of resource groups, subscriptions, and management groups

questions.on: Describe Azure resources and resource groups

questions.on: Describe the hierarchy of resource groups, subscriptions, and management groups
questions.q: A company needs to separate costs and access for two customers it hosts. Which statement is correct?
opts: Neither can separate access
Subscriptions give hard billing and access separation, while resource groups mainly organise resources within one subscription

questions.on: Describe the hierarchy of resource groups, subscriptions, and management groups
questions.q: In the Azure hierarchy, which level directly contains resources such as VMs and databases?

Azure regions
Resource groups
Microsoft Entra tenants

questions.on: Describe management groups

Move the subscription to that division's management group

questions.on: Describe the hierarchy of resource groups, subscriptions, and management groups
questions.q:
Evaluate these statements about inheritance.
1. A role assigned at a management group applies to all subscriptions beneath it.
2. A policy assigned at a resource group applies to resources in that resource group.
3. A policy assigned at a resource group also applies to the parent subscription.

questions.on: Describe management groups
questions.q: A security team wants a single place to apply a company-wide baseline policy to every subscription in the tenant, now and in future. Which scope achieves this?
opts: A resource group named 'global'
The root management group

questions.on: Describe Azure resources and resource groups
questions.q: Is this statement true or false? 'A resource group can contain resources of many different types, such as VMs, databases and networks.'
opts: True, but only if they are in the same availability zone
False. Each resource group can contain only one resource type
True

questions.on: Describe subscriptions
questions.q: A consultant's user account exists in their own company's Entra tenant. They can't be granted access to a client's subscription by searching for their name in the client's directory. Why?

questions.on: Describe subscriptions
questions.q: When you sign up for an Azure free account, what is created for you to deploy resources into?

A management group with no subscriptions

questions.on: Describe Azure resources and resource groups

opts: Yes, based on its region
No. Resource groups themselves are free; you pay for the resources inside them
Only if it has tags

questions.on: Describe Azure resources and resource groups

questions.on: Describe the hierarchy of resource groups, subscriptions, and management groups

False. Subscriptions can't be grouped at all
